chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, that he said:
Regarding a man who left behind two maternal aunts and his freed slaves, he said:
"Those who are related by blood are more entitled to one another."
The wealth is to be divided between the two maternal aunts.

key_terms.أُولُوا الْأَرْحَامِ: blood relatives or kindred who have kinship ties
key_terms.مَوَالِيَهُ: his freed slaves or clients connected by wala'

ai.seo_question: Who inherits first in Shia law: maternal aunts or freed slaves?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on inheritance when a deceased man leaves two maternal aunts and mawali. It affirms, through the Qur'anic principle that blood relatives have greater claim, that the estate belongs to the two maternal aunts rather than the mawali.
